title: Scope revelation evidence to defeasible first-person factual warrant
author: Worldview Sorter AI editorial review
currentBehavior: EPI021@1 is audience-ambiguous and EPI032@1 explicitly asks about the experiencer. The rule combines them under a broad some-justification claim, but excludes EPI032's explicit some answer from support.
proposedBehavior: A new exact first-person, defeasible-initial-reason proposition uses EPI032@1 and EPI122@1. EPI032 substantial/some and EPI122 initial_reason support; EPI032 none and EPI122 investigation_only oppose. Little and depends_on_case remain nondirectional. EPI021 leaves the current public routes and evidence rule but remains historical.
rationale: A reason to investigate a claim is not necessarily a factual reason in favor of its content. The revised question directly distinguishes these accounts for the experiencer without forcing a judgment about an outsider. The existing amount-of-justification vignette supplies complementary but unvalidated authored evidence.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: An apparent divine revelation can sometimes give its experiencer an initial factual reason in favor of its content before independent verification, even if that reason may later be defeated.
nonEntailments: The revelation occurred or is true
Sincerity alone makes the belief justified
The reason is sufficient for settled belief
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: The general reverse-keyed EPI021 has no audience, EPI032 some is omitted from support, and draft EPI120 bundles first-person strength with outsider assessment.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: SEP describes competing arguments and defeaters for religious experience, not a consensus that every apparent revelation justifies belief. First-person grounds and testimonial grounds for hearers are distinct questions.

sourceClaims.claim: A recognized account permits an apparent religious experience to give its subject defeasible initial grounds for a factual belief without independent verification; the subject's grounds and an outsider's testimonial grounds are distinct and disputed.
The epistemic status of putative revelation is disputed; revelation as an apparent communication is distinct from the truth of its content and from its authority for outsiders.

alternatives: Keep EPI021 as directional evidence: rejected because its audience and strength are ambiguous.
Promote draft EPI120 unchanged: rejected because its answers bundle first-person strength with outsider warrant and repeat EPI032's scenario.
Infer substantial standalone warrant from EPI032 some: rejected because that answer explicitly still calls for independent support.
Infer outsider or public warrant: rejected because neither current item asks it directly.
respondentImpact: A respondent can receive an evidence-qualified conclusion about possible, defeasible first-person factual reason. Some current results differ from historical results, which remain reproducible under their release. No respondent is assigned a religion or claim of actual revelation.
historicalCompatibility: Model release 1.12 and its bank, routes, source ledger, catalog, and engine source remain immutable. New administrations use the successor artifacts; old raw responses are not rewritten.

approvals.note: Reviewed SEP sections, audience distinction, provisional versus substantial warrant, ambiguous old item, and explicit non-entailments.

Reviewed exact predecessor paths, new item ID, three same-length route replacements, answer-state distinctions, source bindings, immutable successor paths, and historical replay contract; focused item and pilot validators passed.

release.migration: No raw response migration. Historical administrations retain original manifests. New administrations use EPI122@1 and the scoped rule.
